reasons: The cited text satisfies the rule's preferred position: 19.1 gives a professional/workmanlike services warranty plus material conformity to documentation and specifications; 19.2 gives a 90-day Deliverable conformance warranty measured from the later of delivery or acceptance and continuous conformance for Hosted Services throughout the subscription term (equal to or better than the 12-month software benchmark).

Remedy requirement is met by 19.4 (re-perform/repair/replace, with termination and refund of Fees as a backstop, expressly non-exclusive for fraud, IP, confidentiality, privacy, security and indemnified claims).

Compliance with Applicable Law and no-malicious-code warranties are present in 19.3, and the 19.5 disclaimer is limited to implied warranties and expressly preserves express warranties, service levels, indemnities and remedies, so it does not swallow the express warranty.
The failed deterministic check is a false negative caused by the period being spelled out ("ninety days") rather than expressed numerically; the substantive 90-day period is present.
Consistent with a compliant finding, no redline or counterparty comment is proposed and none is needed; the record is appropriate as internal evaluation evidence.
